newsitem.title: UK: BFB raises upper-tier two capital via dlr Eurobond.
newsitem.headline: BFB raises upper-tier two capital via dlr Eurobond.

text.p: Banco Fonsecas & Burnay's $100 million structured FRN was the first Eurobond from a Portugese bank to qualify as upper-tier two capital, joint lead manager J.P. Morgan said in a statement on Wednesday.

"The combination of the excellent BPI credit story, the rarity of Portugese bank paper and successful pre-marketing led to a very positive reception and firm placement of BFB's issue at launch," J.P. Morgan said.
BFB is a retail banking subsidiary of the Banco Portugues de Investimento group. Today's deal was the first subordinated Eurobond for a BPI entity.
"Since BPI's purchase of BFB in 1991 the turnaround in its operations has been remarkable," the statement said.
Caixa Geral de Depositos is joint lead manager.

BFB's subordinated perpetual step-up callable FRN pays an initial coupon of three-month LIBOR plus 70 basis points. The bond is callable after five years and if it is not called, the coupon steps-up to three-month LIBOR plus 220 b.p.
BFB is Portugal's highest rated bank, with an A2 senior rating from Moody's Investors Service and A+ rating from IBCA.
It said a successful European roadshow created widespread demand for BFB's issue from European pension funds, banks and insurance companies.
It said the money would be used to finance BPI's purchase of Banco Fomento Exterior in August.
